idiom_name: Grule: GRL rules compiled into a KnowledgeBase, facts in a DataContext
implementation_notes: Grule is Go's rule engine: rules are written in GRL (rule <name> with a when section and a then section), compiled into a KnowledgeBase and executed against facts in a DataContext. Facts are pointers to your own structs - or JSON added with AddJSON - so rule expressions read your Go fields, but only exported ones and only 64-bit numeric types. Salience orders conflicting rules, and because matching is data-driven there is no textual order to rely on; every action that changes what its condition matched should Retract (or flag Changed) so the engine converges. Build the KnowledgeBase once at startup and clone a per-request instance from it, since loading rules is expensive and an instance carries its own working memory.
pitfalls: GRL resolves only exported (capitalised) fields and 64-bit numeric types: an unexported field or an int32 silently fails to resolve, and out-of-range array access panics.
A rule that does not Retract itself re-matches the facts it changed; grule reports this as a failure to converge rather than looping forever, but the rule set is still wrong.
A KnowledgeBase instance owns its working memory and is not safe to execute concurrently - clone one instance per goroutine or request.
Rule loading is not free (grule's own benchmark: 1000 rules load in roughly a second and use hundreds of megabytes), so build the blueprint once and clone instances per evaluation.
